description: Experiment 15B, semantic variant (session-2 plan P42; R-b load): query-api ECS scale-out and scale-in driven by POST /v1/semantic/retrieve (public API-key route, P40) through load-tests/loadgen.py at concurrency 1, 5, 25 and 50, then a sustained hold at 50 and a 30-minute no-load observation window. A warm-up pass first sends each of the 150 fixed DBLP topic phrases once at concurrency 1, so Voyage is called at most once per distinct question per semantic-service task (query-embedding cache, P40). Each request does real work: query-api forwards to semantic-service, which embeds the question (cache) and queries one S3 Vectors index. No LLM answers are sent. Per-level request limits are REQUIRED and are the S3 Vectors cost bound of R-b: 600 / 3,000 / 15,000 / 30,000 / 150,000 (198,600 in total, plus the warm-up of at most 200); they must not be raised.

scaling_policy.type: ECS service target tracking on ECSServiceAverageCPUUtilization (standard AWS/ECS metric; Container Insights is off), plus, when the P41 variable query_requests_per_target_target is set, ALBRequestCountPerTarget (query-api only)
scaling_policy.target_percent_reference: cpu_target_percent in infra/terraform/phase12b-variables.tf (default 60); read the applied value before the run, it is not in this file
scaling_policy.scale_in_alarm: AWS-managed low alarm needs 15 consecutive one-minute datapoints under 90 percent of the target, so scale-in cannot start before about 15 minutes of low CPU
scaling_policy.capacity_source: service_capacity.query-api in the private tfvars (the example file has min 1, max 2); confirm with aws application-autoscaling describe-scalable-targets before the run
scaling_policy.fargate_shape: 0.25 vCPU / 1 GiB, raised only in private tfvars
scaling_policy.request_count_policy: exists only when query_requests_per_target_target is set in the runtime tfvars (value from the P35 rehearsal); read the applied value and policy before the run, they are not in this file
scaling_policy.rate_limit_reference: SCHOLARCHAIN_SEMANTIC_RATE_LIMIT_PER_SECOND / _BURST on query-api (P40 code defaults 50 / 100; query_semantic_rate_limit_per_second and _burst, P41); the Session 2 value is set from P35 so that no level is throttled; read the applied values before the run

phases.name: warmup
phases.purpose: warm-up: each of the 150 distinct questions sent once, in file order, one worker; embed calls then equal the distinct questions per semantic-service task. Its own phase, so cold-cache latency stays out of the level-1 baseline. The phase ends after one pass; 600 s is only the upper bound

phases.name: baseline-1
phases.purpose: baseline CPU, latency and task count at concurrency 1 (warm cache)

phases.name: hold-50
phases.purpose: sustain concurrency 50 for 10 minutes so the request rate stays above the target for the datapoints a scale-out needs and the new task has time to start (health-check grace 300 s)

phases.name: cooldown-observe
phases.purpose: no load for 30 minutes (at least 25 quiet minutes): scale-in needs 15 low minutes plus the 300 s cooldown; evidence is the metric rows before, during and after, collected outside this process

llm.note: No LLM answers: this manifest sends none (llm_answers 0 everywhere) and --llm is refused with it. The only external call behind the load is Voyage query embedding on cache misses (at most the distinct questions per semantic-service task, session-2 plan section 6.3a), read from the Voyage usage page after the run, not from this process.

metrics_to_collect.note: the metric the P41 request-count policy tracks; it includes 429 replies, so with zero 429s it equals the served requests
429 replies from the query-api rate limiter appear here; the load generator reports them per level
the task count over time as a standard metric: 1 to 2 is the scale-out, 2 back to 1 the scale-in
Container Insights is off, so AWS/ECS RunningTaskCount does not exist; poll the service every minute with UTC timestamps
start and end time and cause of each scale-out and scale-in

metrics_to_collect.metric: target tracking alarm state changes for query-api
per-request latency, status and route with run IDs; per level: successful_requests, success_rps, peak_success_rps_1s, rate_limited_429
metrics_to_collect.note: target/experiment-runs/15b-ecs-scaling-semantic-<run-id>/raw/ (sha256 sealed); derived/summary.json and timeline.csv (one row per UTC minute, with successful_requests and rate_limited_429). 429 replies are counted per level and excluded from latency, throughput and success rate.

provenance.requirements: docs/runbooks/session-2-plan.md rows P42, P35 and P40, sections 6.3a and 5.3 (required per-level limits, warm-up, 429 separation); questions: experiments/inputs/15b/semantic-questions.provenance.json
provenance.run: python3 -I load-tests/loadgen.py run --manifest experiments/manifests/15b-ecs-scaling-semantic.json --questions-file experiments/inputs/15b/semantic-questions.txt --run-id <run-id> (no --node-ids-file, --evidence-ids-file or --llm; commands in experiments/README.md)

limits_note: The per-level limits 600 / 3,000 / 15,000 / 30,000 / 150,000 are the R-b cost bound and must not be raised; load-tests/loadgen.py and experiments/scripts/check_manifests.py refuse a manifest above them. A 429 counts toward its phase limit. Known limitation to report: query-api max is 2 tasks, so scale-out is 1 to 2 only. If neither policy scales out at concurrency 50, report that and the measured values rather than tuning the service or the target inside the run.
